# GK Quiz Platform — Implementation Plan

A full-featured **General Knowledge Quiz Platform** built with **Next.js** (App Router) and **local JSON-based storage**. Features admin quiz management, user accounts, auto-question generation from URLs, timed quizzes, score tracking, and a leaderboard — all wrapped in a sleek dark theme with vibrant accents.

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Auto-Question Generation from URLs**: This feature will use a simple web-scraping + keyword-extraction approach to generate quiz questions from a given URL. It extracts key sentences and converts them into questions. This is a best-effort heuristic — it won't produce perfect questions every time, but gives a solid starting point that you can then edit in the admin panel.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication**: User accounts will use a simple local JSON-based auth system with hashed passwords (bcrypt). This is suitable for local/personal use. For production deployment, you'd want to add a proper auth provider (NextAuth.js, etc.).

> [!NOTE]
> **Admin Account**: On first launch, the app will auto-create an admin account with credentials you define in an environment variable (`.env.local`). You'll be the only admin.

---

## Open Questions

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Admin Credentials**: Do you want the default admin login to be something like `admin` / `admin123`, or would you prefer to set custom credentials? (You can always change them later.)

> [!NOTE]
> **Quiz URL Scraping**: The URL-to-quiz feature will work best with text-heavy pages (Wikipedia, news articles, blog posts). JavaScript-rendered single-page apps may not scrape well. Is that acceptable?

---

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[User Browser] -->|Next.js App| B[Frontend - React Pages]
    B --> C[API Routes - Next.js]
    C --> D[JSON File Storage]
    C --> E[URL Scraper + Question Generator]
    
    subgraph Pages
        B1[Home / Landing]
        B2[Quiz Browser]
        B3[Quiz Player]
        B4[Leaderboard]
        B5[Login / Register]
        B6[Admin Dashboard]
        B7[Admin Quiz Editor]
    end
    
    subgraph Storage
        D1[users.json]
        D2[quizzes.json]
        D3[scores.json]
    end
    
    B --> B1 & B2 & B3 & B4 & B5 & B6 & B7
    D --> D1 & D2 & D3
```

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Framework | Next.js 14+ (App Router) |
| Language | TypeScript |
| Styling | Vanilla CSS (dark theme, glassmorphism, gradients) |
| Storage | Local JSON files (via `fs` in API routes) |
| Auth | bcryptjs for password hashing, JWT tokens via cookies |
| Scraping | `cheerio` for HTML parsing (URL → questions) |
| Icons | Lucide React |
| Fonts | Google Fonts (Inter / Outfit) |

---

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Project Setup & Configuration

#### [NEW] `gk-quiz-platform/` (project root)

Initialize with `npx create-next-app@latest` using TypeScript, App Router, and no Tailwind.

#### [NEW] `.env.local`
- `ADMIN_USERNAME=admin`
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123`
- `JWT_SECRET=<random-string>`

---

### 2. Data Layer

#### [NEW] `src/lib/db.ts`
JSON file-based CRUD operations for users, quizzes, and scores. Uses `fs` to read/write JSON files in a `data/` directory.

#### [NEW] `src/lib/auth.ts`
- Password hashing with bcryptjs
- JWT token creation & verification
- Middleware helper to protect admin routes

#### [NEW] `src/lib/types.ts`
TypeScript interfaces:
- `User` — id, username, passwordHash, role (admin/user), createdAt
- `Quiz` — id, title, description, category, questions[], createdAt, updatedAt
- `Question` — id, type (mcq/truefalse/fillinblank), questionText, options[], correctAnswer, explanation
- `Score` — id, userId, quizId, score, totalQuestions, timeTaken, completedAt

#### [NEW] `data/users.json`, `data/quizzes.json`, `data/scores.json`
Initial empty JSON arrays (auto-seeded with admin user on first run).

---

### 3. API Routes

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
POST — Register a new user account.

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts`
POST — Login, returns JWT token as httpOnly cookie.

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts`
POST — Clear auth cookie.

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/auth/me/route.ts`
GET — Return current logged-in user info.

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/quizzes/route.ts`
GET — List all quizzes (with optional category filter).
POST — Create a new quiz (admin only).

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/quizzes/[id]/route.ts`
GET — Get quiz by ID.
PUT — Update quiz (admin only).
DELETE — Delete quiz (admin only).

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/quizzes/generate/route.ts`
POST — Accept a URL, scrape content, generate quiz questions using heuristic NLP.

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/scores/route.ts`
GET — Get leaderboard / user scores.
POST — Submit a quiz score.

#### [NEW] `src/app/api/admin/seed/route.ts`
POST — Seed admin account on first run.

---

### 4. URL → Quiz Question Generator

#### [NEW] `src/lib/question-generator.ts`
1. Fetch HTML from the given URL
2. Parse with `cheerio` — extract main text content (paragraphs, headings)
3. Split into sentences, identify key factual statements
4. Generate question types:
   - **MCQ**: Replace key entity with blank, generate 3 distractors
   - **True/False**: Slightly alter a fact and ask if it's true
   - **Fill-in-the-blank**: Remove a key word from a sentence
5. Return an array of generated `Question` objects for admin review/editing

---

### 5. Frontend Pages

#### [NEW] `src/app/page.tsx` — Landing Page
- Hero section with animated gradient background
- Stats cards (total quizzes, users, questions answered)
- Featured quizzes carousel
- Call-to-action buttons

#### [NEW] `src/app/quizzes/page.tsx` — Quiz Browser
- Grid of quiz cards with category filters
- Search functionality
- Category tags with color coding
- Difficulty indicators

#### [NEW] `src/app/quizzes/[id]/page.tsx` — Quiz Player
- Question display with smooth transitions
- Countdown timer (configurable per quiz)
- Progress bar
- Answer selection with instant visual feedback (correct = green glow, wrong = red shake)
- Results screen with score breakdown

#### [NEW] `src/app/leaderboard/page.tsx` — Leaderboard
- Global rankings table
- Filter by quiz / category
- User avatars (generated initials)
- Animated rank badges (🥇🥈🥉)

#### [NEW] `src/app/login/page.tsx` — Login Page
- Glassmorphism card design
- Login / Register toggle

#### [NEW] `src/app/admin/page.tsx` — Admin Dashboard
- Overview stats (total quizzes, questions, users, scores)
- Quick actions (create quiz, generate from URL)
- Recent activity feed

#### [NEW] `src/app/admin/quizzes/page.tsx` — Admin Quiz List
- Table of all quizzes with edit/delete actions
- Bulk operations

#### [NEW] `src/app/admin/quizzes/new/page.tsx` — Create/Edit Quiz
- Quiz metadata form (title, description, category)
- Question editor with drag-and-drop reorder
- Add question types (MCQ, T/F, Fill-in-blank)
- URL input field to auto-generate questions
- Preview mode

---

### 6. Shared Components

#### [NEW] `src/components/Navbar.tsx`
- Logo + nav links
- User avatar dropdown (login/logout/admin)
- Mobile hamburger menu
- Glass effect on scroll

#### [NEW] `src/components/QuizCard.tsx`
- Hover lift animation
- Category badge
- Question count & estimated time
- Gradient border effect

#### [NEW] `src/components/Timer.tsx`
- Circular countdown with SVG animation
- Color transitions (green → yellow → red)

#### [NEW] `src/components/QuestionDisplay.tsx`
- Renders different question types
- Answer selection with animations
- Explanation reveal after answering

#### [NEW] `src/components/ScoreCard.tsx`
- Animated score reveal
- Circular progress ring
- Grade badge (A+, A, B, etc.)

#### [NEW] `src/components/AdminSidebar.tsx`
- Collapsible sidebar navigation
- Active state indicators

---

### 7. Styling

#### [NEW] `src/app/globals.css`
Design system with:
- **Colors**: Dark backgrounds (`#0a0a0f`, `#12121a`), vibrant accents (electric blue `#6366f1`, purple `#8b5cf6`, emerald `#10b981`)
- **Glassmorphism**: `backdrop-filter: blur()` with semi-transparent backgrounds
- **Gradients**: Multi-stop gradients for buttons, cards, and backgrounds
- **Animations**: Fade-in, slide-up, pulse, shake, glow keyframes
- **Typography**: Inter/Outfit from Google Fonts
- **Responsive**: Mobile-first breakpoints

---

## File Structure

```
gk-quiz-platform/
├── data/                          # JSON storage
│   ├── users.json
│   ├── quizzes.json
│   └── scores.json
├── public/                        # Static assets
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── globals.css            # Design system
│   │   ├── layout.tsx             # Root layout
│   │   ├── page.tsx               # Landing page
│   │   ├── login/page.tsx         # Auth page
│   │   ├── quizzes/
│   │   │   ├── page.tsx           # Quiz browser
│   │   │   └── [id]/page.tsx      # Quiz player
│   │   ├── leaderboard/page.tsx   # Leaderboard
│   │   ├── admin/
│   │   │   ├── page.tsx           # Admin dashboard
│   │   │   └── quizzes/
│   │   │       ├── page.tsx       # Quiz list
│   │   │       └── new/page.tsx   # Create/edit quiz
│   │   └── api/
│   │       ├── auth/
│   │       │   ├── register/route.ts
│   │       │   ├── login/route.ts
│   │       │   ├── logout/route.ts
│   │       │   └── me/route.ts
│   │       ├── quizzes/
│   │       │   ├── route.ts
│   │       │   ├── [id]/route.ts
│   │       │   └── generate/route.ts
│   │       ├── scores/route.ts
│   │       └── admin/seed/route.ts
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── Navbar.tsx
│   │   ├── QuizCard.tsx
│   │   ├── Timer.tsx
│   │   ├── QuestionDisplay.tsx
│   │   ├── ScoreCard.tsx
│   │   └── AdminSidebar.tsx
│   └── lib/
│       ├── db.ts                  # JSON file operations
│       ├── auth.ts                # Auth utilities
│       ├── types.ts               # TypeScript interfaces
│       └── question-generator.ts  # URL → questions
├── .env.local
├── package.json
└── next.config.js
```

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Checks
- `npm run build` — Ensure the project compiles without errors
- `npm run dev` — Start dev server and verify all pages render

### Manual Verification
1. **Auth flow**: Register a new user, login, verify protected routes
2. **Admin panel**: Create a quiz manually, edit it, delete it
3. **URL generation**: Paste a Wikipedia URL, verify questions are generated
4. **Quiz play**: Take a quiz, verify timer, scoring, and answer feedback
5. **Leaderboard**: Verify scores appear after completing quizzes
6. **Responsive**: Test on mobile viewport sizes
7. **Dark theme**: Verify all pages use the dark design consistently

1: # GK Quiz Platform — Implementation Plan
2: 
3: A full-featured **General Knowledge Quiz Platform** built with **Next.js** (App Router) and **local JSON-based storage**. Features admin quiz management, user accounts, auto-question generation from URLs, timed quizzes, score tracking, and a leaderboard — all wrapped in a sleek dark theme with vibrant accents.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## User Review Required
8: 
9: > [!IMPORTANT]
10: > **Auto-Question Generation from URLs**: This feature will use a simple web-scraping + keyword-extraction approach to generate quiz questions from a given URL. It extracts key sentences and converts them into questions. This is a best-effort heuristic — it won't produce perfect questions every time, but gives a solid starting point that you can then edit in the admin panel.
11: 
12: > [!IMPORTANT]
13: > **Authentication**: User accounts will use a simple local JSON-based auth system with hashed passwords (bcrypt). This is suitable for local/personal use. For production deployment, you'd want to add a proper auth provider (NextAuth.js, etc.).
14: 
15: > [!NOTE]
16: > **Admin Account**: On first launch, the app will auto-create an admin account with credentials you define in an environment variable (`.env.local`). You'll be the only admin.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## Open Questions
21: 
22: > [!IMPORTANT]
23: > **Admin Credentials**: Do you want the default admin login to be something like `admin` / `admin123`, or would you prefer to set custom credentials? (You can always change them later.)
24: 
25: > [!NOTE]
26: > **Quiz URL Scraping**: The URL-to-quiz feature will work best with text-heavy pages (Wikipedia, news articles, blog posts). JavaScript-rendered single-page apps may not scrape well. Is that acceptable?
27:

# ALA QUIZPEDIA - New Features Implementation Plan

We are adding four powerful new features to the **ALA QUIZPEDIA** platform:
1. **Google AI Question Generator**: Directly uses the Google Gemini API (2.5-flash) in the client to generate high-quality MCQ, True/False, and Fill-in-the-blank questions.
2. **Bulk Images Adder**: Upload images (stored as Base64 or URLs) in a centralized gallery and attach them to quizzes and individual questions.
3. **Import/Export JSON File**: Save/back up your database of quizzes, scores, and users into a local `.json` file, and upload it back to restore data.
4. **URL Generator**: Get shareable direct links for individual quizzes with customizable play options.

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Gemini API Key Security**: The Gemini API key will be entered directly in the admin panel and stored locally in your browser's `localStorage`. It is never uploaded to any external server except directly to Google's official endpoints.

> [!WARNING]
> **LocalStorage Storage Limits**: Because this is a static client-side web application, files are stored inside the browser's `localStorage` (typically capped at 5-10MB). Storing too many high-resolution Base64 images will exceed this limit. We recommend using **Image URLs** where possible, or keeping Base64 uploads compressed/small.

---

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Google AI Integration
#### [MODIFY] [quiz-generator.js](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/js/quiz-generator.js)
* Add a `generateQuestionsWithGemini(apiKey, topic, count)` function.
* It sends a direct REST request to the Gemini API (`gemini-2.5-flash`) using a system prompt that enforces outputting valid JSON questions fitting our exact schema.
* Integrates seamlessly as the primary generator in the UI when an API key is saved.

### 2. Bulk Images Gallery
#### [MODIFY] [storage.js](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/js/storage.js)
* Expand the database schema to include `images` (array of `{ id, name, url/base64 }`).
* Add functions to add, retrieve, and delete images from the gallery.
* Update `Quiz` and `Question` interfaces to support an optional `image` field.

#### [NEW] [admin-images.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-images.html)
* A dedicated dashboard page to upload multiple images at once (using drag & drop or URL input) and view the image gallery.

### 3. Import / Export JSON Database
#### [MODIFY] [admin.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin.html)
* Add a "Database Settings" section containing:
  - **Export JSON**: Downloads a full database dump (`alaquizpedia_db.json`).
  - **Import JSON**: Uploads a JSON file to restore all quizzes, scores, and users.

### 4. Direct Play URL Generator
#### [MODIFY] [admin-quizzes.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-quizzes.html)
* Add a "Share Link" button next to each quiz.
* Open a modal with copyable URL (e.g. `http://domain.com/quiz-player.html?id=quiz-id`).
* Add toggle options to disable timers, set a fixed username, or enable instant answers, appending query params (e.g. `&timer=disabled`) which `quiz-player.html` will respect.

### 5. UI Updates
#### [MODIFY] [admin-quiz-edit.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-quiz-edit.html)
* Add a Gemini API Key input field (stored securely in localStorage).
* Add image selectors (from gallery or URL) to the Quiz details and to each Question editor block.
* Display thumbnails of selected images.

#### [MODIFY] [quiz-player.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/quiz-player.html)
* Update question display card to show images prominently if attached.
* Respect custom URL generator query parameters.

---

## Verification Plan
1. **Google AI**: Add a Gemini API Key, enter a topic like "Nuclear Physics", and verify 10 distinct questions are successfully created.
2. **Bulk Images**: Upload 3 images, attach one to a quiz, one to a question, and verify they render inside `quiz-player.html` and `quizzes.html`.
3. **Import/Export**: Export database to JSON, clear browser data, import JSON, and confirm database is fully restored.
4. **URL Gen**: Generate a shareable URL, paste it in a new window, and confirm it plays the correct quiz.

# ALA QUIZPEDIA — Features Walkthrough

All the requested features have been successfully implemented! Here is a guide on how everything works:

## 1. 🤖 Google AI Question Generator (Gemini Integration)
The platform now uses Google Gemini (2.5-flash) to automatically generate questions based on any topic.
- **Where to find it:** Head over to the **Admin Panel** > **Manage Quizzes** > **Create New Quiz**.
- **How it works:**
  1. Expand the "Auto-Generate with Google Gemini AI" section.
  2. Input your **Google Gemini API Key** and click "Save Key" (it will be saved to your browser so you don't have to enter it again).
  3. Enter a topic (e.g., "Ancient Rome", "JavaScript Basics").
  4. Specify the number of questions, difficulty, and type.
  5. Click "Generate via Gemini". The AI will stream the generated questions directly into your quiz editor!

## 2. 🖼 Bulk Images Management
You can now upload images and assign them to quizzes (as cover images) or to individual questions.
- **Where to find it:** In the **Admin Panel**, click the new **"🖼 Manage Images"** link in the sidebar to open the Gallery.
- **How it works:**
  1. Upload multiple image files (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP) up to 2MB each.
  2. The images are stored in your local storage database as Base64 strings.
  3. You can view, rename, and delete these images from the gallery.
  4. **Using Images:** When editing a quiz, you will now see dropdown menus to select a **Quiz Cover Image** and a **Question Image** for each individual question. These images will be beautifully displayed on the quiz cards and during gameplay.

## 3. 💾 Database Import / Export (JSON)
Since all data is stored in the browser's LocalStorage, you can now backup your entire platform or migrate it to another browser/device.
- **Where to find it:** On the main **Admin Panel** dashboard (`admin.html`).
- **How it works:**
  - **Export DB:** Click to download a `quizpedia_backup.json` file containing all your users, quizzes, scores, and images.
  - **Import DB:** Upload a previously exported JSON file to completely restore your platform's state. *Warning: This overwrites your current database!*

## 4. 🔗 Share URL Generator
You can easily share direct links to specific quizzes with your players.
- **Where to find it:** In the **Admin Panel** > **Manage Quizzes**.
- **How it works:**
  - Click the **"Share"** button next to any quiz.
  - A modal will pop up generating the exact URL (e.g., `quiz-player.html?id=q-12345`).
  - Click "Copy Link" to quickly copy it to your clipboard.

> [!TIP]
> Since this is a client-side application using LocalStorage, make sure you Export your database occasionally, especially if you add large images, to ensure your content is safely backed up.

### How to Test It Now:
1. Open [`admin.html`](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin.html) in your browser.
2. Log in using your admin credentials (Username: `admin`, Password: `Admin@1234`).
3. Upload some images in the Gallery.
4. Try generating a quiz with your Gemini API Key.
5. Apply your uploaded images to the new quiz and try playing it!

Because this is a plain static site, you can leave the **build command** blank and set the **publish directory** to `.`. #### 3.4 Deploy *One‑time deploy (preview):* ```powershell netlify deploy --dir=. --open ``` *Production deploy (makes the URL permanent):* ```powershell netlify deploy --dir=. --prod ``` You’ll see a URL like `https://my‑quiz‑site.netlify.app`. ## 2️⃣ Deploy via Netlify CLI (recommended for ongoing development)

### 2.1 Install the CLI (once)

netlify login

netlify link --id <site‑id>

```powershell
netlify sites:create --name my-quiz-site
```

  This will output a new Site ID; keep it handy.

```powershell
netlify deploy \
  --dir "C:\Users\Anandhy\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\gk-quiz-platform" \
  --prod   # deploys to the production URL
```

The CLI will show a preview URL first. If everything looks good, confirm the production deploy.

Create a file `netlify.toml` in the project root (same folder) with:

```toml
[build]

  publish = "."   # publish the root folder

[[redirects]]
  from = "/*"
  to = "/index.html"
  status = 200
```

This tells Netlify to serve `index.html` for any route (useful if you later add client‑side routing).

### 2.6 Set up continuous deployment (Git) – optional but handy

### 1️⃣ **Drag‑and‑Drop deploy (no installation needed)**  

1. Open the **Netlify Dashboard** in your browser.

> **Pros:** Instant, no command‑line tools required.  
> **Cons:** You’ll need to repeat the drag‑and‑drop for every future change.

---

### 2️⃣ **Deploy with the Netlify CLI (once Node is installed)**  

If you prefer a command‑line workflow for continuous updates:

1. **Install Node.js (includes npm)**  
   *Download the Windows installer* from https://nodejs.org (LTS version) and run it.  
   After installation, open a new PowerShell window and verify:

   ```powershell
   node -v
   npm -v
   ```

2. **Install the Netlify CLI**  

   ```powershell
   npm install -g netlify-cli
   ```

3. **Log in to Netlify**

   ```powershell
   netlify login
   ```

4. **Create (or link) a site**

   ```powershell
   # create a brand‑new site
   netlify sites:create --name gk-quiz-platform-$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMddHHmmss)

   # or, if you already have a site, link to it:
   netlify link --id <existing‑site‑id>
   ```

5. **Deploy the static folder**

   ```powershell
   netlify deploy `
     --dir "C:\Users\Anandhy\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\gk-quiz-platform" `
     --prod
   ```

   The CLI will first show a **draft URL**; confirm to push to the production URL.

6. (Optional) **Add a `netlify.toml`** to the project root so future builds work automatically:

   ```toml
   [build]
     publish = "."   # root folder

   [[redirects]]
     from = "/*"
     to = "/index.html"
     status = 200
   ```

7. **Continuous deployment (Git)** – if you later push the repo to GitHub and connect it in Netlify, every `git push` will automatically trigger a new deploy without any manual steps.

import os
import zipfile
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
import json
import io

def create_zip_of_directory(directory_path):
    print(f"Zipping {directory_path}...")
    mem_zip = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(mem_zip, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory_path):
            # Exclude the script itself and any hidden folders like .git if they exist
            if '.git' in root or '__pycache__' in root:
                continue
            for file in files:
                if file == "deploy_netlify.py":
                    continue
                file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
                arcname = os.path.relpath(file_path, directory_path)
                zf.write(file_path, arcname)
    return mem_zip.getvalue()

def deploy_to_netlify(token, site_name, directory_path):
    zip_data = create_zip_of_directory(directory_path)

    # 1. Create a new site
    print("Creating new Netlify site...")
    create_site_url = "https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    
    data = {"name": site_name} if site_name else {}
    
    req = urllib.request.Request(create_site_url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(data).encode('utf-8'), method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
            site_info = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
            site_id = site_info['id']
            site_url = site_info['ssl_url']
            print(f"Site created successfully! ID: {site_id}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        err_msg = e.read().decode('utf-8')
        print(f"Failed to create site: {err_msg}")
        if "name" in err_msg and "taken" in err_msg:
            print("That site name is already taken. Try leaving it blank for a random name, or pick a unique one.")
        return

    # 2. Deploy to the site using the zip upload API
    print("Deploying files to Netlify...")
    deploy_url = f"https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites/{site_id}/deploys"
    deploy_headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/zip"
    }
    
    req_deploy = urllib.request.Request(deploy_url, headers=deploy_headers, data=zip_data, method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_deploy) as response:
            deploy_info = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
            print("-" * 40)
            print("🚀 DEPLOYMENT SUCCESSFUL! 🚀")
            print(f"Your site is live at: {site_url}")
            print("-" * 40)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        print(f"Failed to deploy: {e.read().decode('utf-8')}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- Netlify Python Deployer ---")
    print("To use this, you need a Netlify Personal Access Token.")
    print("You can generate one here: https://app.netlify.com/user/applications#personal-access-tokens")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    token = input("Enter your Netlify Token: ").strip()
    if not token:
        print("Token is required! Exiting...")
        exit(1)
        
    site_name = input("Enter a site name (optional, leave blank for random): ").strip()
    
    current_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    deploy_to_netlify(token, site_name, current_dir)

import os
import zipfile
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
import json
import io

def create_zip_of_directory(directory_path):
    print(f"Zipping {directory_path}...")
    mem_zip = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(mem_zip, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory_path):
            # Exclude the script itself and any hidden folders like .git if they exist
            if '.git' in root or '__pycache__' in root:
                continue
            for file in files:
                if file == "deploy_netlify.py":
                    continue
                file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
                arcname = os.path.relpath(file_path, directory_path)
                zf.write(file_path, arcname)
    return mem_zip.getvalue()

def deploy_to_netlify(token, site_name, directory_path):
    zip_data = create_zip_of_directory(directory_path)

    # 1. Create a new site
    print("Creating new Netlify site...")
    create_site_url = "https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    
    data = {"name": site_name} if site_name else {}
    
    req = urllib.request.Request(create_site_url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(data).encode('utf-8'), method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
            site_info = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
            site_id = site_info['id']
            site_url = site_info['ssl_url']
            print(f"Site created successfully! ID: {site_id}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        err_msg = e.read().decode('utf-8')
        print(f"Failed to create site: {err_msg}")
        if "name" in err_msg and "taken" in err_msg:
            print("That site name is already taken. Try leaving it blank for a random name, or pick a unique one.")
        return

    # 2. Deploy to the site using the zip upload API
    print("Deploying files to Netlify...")
    deploy_url = f"https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites/{site_id}/deploys"
    deploy_headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/zip"
    }
    
    req_deploy = urllib.request.Request(deploy_url, headers=deploy_headers, data=zip_data, method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_deploy) as response:
            deploy_info = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
            print("-" * 40)
            print("🚀 DEPLOYMENT SUCCESSFUL! 🚀")
            print(f"Your site is live at: {site_url}")
            print("-" * 40)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        print(f"Failed to deploy: {e.read().decode('utf-8')}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- Netlify Python Deployer ---")
    print("To use this, you need a Netlify Personal Access Token.")
    print("You can generate one here: https://app.netlify.com/user/applications#personal-access-tokens")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    token = input("Enter your Netlify Token: ").strip()
    if not token:
        print("Token is required! Exiting...")
        exit(1)
        
    site_name = input("Enter a site name (optional, leave blank for random): ").strip()
    
    current_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    deploy_to_netlify(token, site_name, current_dir)

# Implementation Plan – User Study Materials, Admin User Performance, Admin-Free Leaderboard & Python Question Importer

Implement user-facing study materials, detailed admin tracking for registered users' performance, exclude admin from user leaderboards, and provide a Python question import utility.

## Proposed Changes

### Storage & Utility Layer
#### [MODIFY] [storage.js](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/js/storage.js)
- Update `getLeaderboard()` to filter out users with `role === 'admin'` or `username === 'admin'`.
- Add `getUserPerformanceSummary(userId)` helper to compute total attempts, average score %, highest score %, and detailed history per user.
- Add `getStudyMaterials()` helper to fetch materials for public display.

---

### User-Facing Study Materials
#### [NEW] [materials.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/materials.html)
- Create public study materials page for all users (Notes, Links, Videos, PDFs).
- Includes category and type filter buttons, search bar, and reader modal.

#### [MODIFY] Navigation Links across HTML files:
- [index.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/index.html)
- [quizzes.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/quizzes.html)
- [leaderboard.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/leaderboard.html)
- [login.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/login.html)
- Add "Study Materials" / "📖 Materials" link to navbar.

---

### Admin User Tracking & Performance View
#### [MODIFY] [admin-users.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-users.html)
- Add user performance statistics (Total attempts, Avg score %, Best score %).
- Add "📊 View Performance" action button for each registered user.
- Add modal showing detailed performance breakdown for a selected user (Quiz title, score, accuracy %, time taken, timestamp).

---

### Leaderboard & Topper Summary
#### [MODIFY] [leaderboard.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/leaderboard.html)
- Exclude admin scores/accounts from leaderboard and podium.
- Add **Topper Summary Card** at top highlighting #1 Topper, Best Accuracy, and Most Active Quizzer.

---

### Python Question Importer Tool
#### [NEW] [import_questions.py](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/import_questions.py)
- Python CLI tool to load JSON files containing quiz questions, validate fields, and merge them into `seed_data.json` / site data.
- Also generates a `seed_data.json` so site automatically loads imported quizzes if present.

#### [NEW] [sample_questions.json](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/sample_questions.json)
- Template JSON file with sample quizzes and questions for Python import.

## Verification Plan

### Automated / Script Verification
- Run `python import_questions.py --sample` to test importing questions.

### Manual Verification
- Test `materials.html` as regular user and guest.
- Test `admin-users.html` to view performance of registered users.
- Test `leaderboard.html` to confirm admins are excluded and toppers are displayed correctly.

# Implementation Plan – User Study Materials, Shared User Performance, JSON Importer & Admin Control

Implement public study materials, shared user performance stats among users (excluding admin), admin-only quiz and user management, persistent user accounts, and Python JSON question importer.

## Key Rules & Access Controls

1. **Admin Only**:
   - Create, edit, delete quizzes (`admin-quizzes.html`, `admin-quiz-edit.html`).
   - Create, edit, delete study materials (`admin-materials.html`).
   - Manage users and delete accounts (`admin-users.html`).
   - Database backup/restore & reset (`admin-data.html`).

2. **All Users (Regular Users & Public)**:
   - Access all Quizzes (`quizzes.html`, `quiz-player.html`).
   - Access all Study Materials (`materials.html`).
   - Access Leaderboard & view **each other's performance statistics** (`leaderboard.html`).
   - Admin's account and scores are excluded from the public leaderboard.
   - User accounts created by registration or admin remain active and persistent until Admin explicitly deletes them.

3. **Python & JSON Data Import/Export**:
   - Python script (`import_questions.py`) to import/export quiz questions via JSON.
   - Web JSON import/export in `admin-data.html`.

## Proposed Changes

### Storage & Data Layer
#### [MODIFY] [storage.js](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/js/storage.js)
- Ensure all user accounts and scores persist safely without unintended overrides.
- Exclude `admin` from `getLeaderboard()`.
- Add functions to aggregate and retrieve shared user performance statistics.

### Public Pages

- User-facing Study Materials page (Notes, Links, Videos, PDFs).

#### [MODIFY] [leaderboard.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/leaderboard.html)
- Display all user performances and toppers (excluding admin).
- Add user performance detail modal so users can view each other's achievements.

#### [MODIFY] Navbars across pages:
- Add "Study Materials" to navbar in `index.html`, `quizzes.html`, `leaderboard.html`, `materials.html`, `login.html`.

### Admin Pages
#### [MODIFY] [admin-users.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-users.html)
- Admin user control table with detailed user attempt history and performance inspection.
- Explicit account protection so user accounts are never lost unless Admin deletes them.

### Python Tools
#### [NEW] [import_questions.py](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/import_questions.py)
- Python tool to import and export quiz questions to/from JSON.

#### [NEW] [sample_questions.json](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/sample_questions.json)
- Sample JSON file format for questions import.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
================================================
import_questions.py — ALA QUIZPEDIA Question Importer
Created for A.SHAM SHARAN
================================================
Use this Python script to validate, format, and package quiz questions
from JSON files into the ALA QUIZPEDIA database format.
"""

import sys
import os
import json
import random
import time

def validate_quiz(quiz):
    """Validate that a quiz dict has all required fields."""
    errors = []
    if not isinstance(quiz, dict):
        return ["Quiz item must be a JSON object"]
    
    if not quiz.get("title"):
        errors.append("Missing quiz title")
    
    questions = quiz.get("questions")
    if not isinstance(questions, list) or len(questions) == 0:
        errors.append("Quiz must contain at least one question in 'questions' array")
    else:
        for idx, q in enumerate(questions):
            if not q.get("question"):
                errors.append(f"Question #{idx+1}: Missing question text")
            options = q.get("options")
            if not isinstance(options, list) or len(options) < 2:
                errors.append(f"Question #{idx+1}: Must have at least 2 options")
            correct = q.get("correct")
            if not isinstance(correct, int) or correct < 0 or (options and correct >= len(options)):
                errors.append(f"Question #{idx+1}: 'correct' index out of range (must be 0 to {len(options)-1 if options else 0})")
    
    return errors

def import_questions(file_path, output_path=None):
    """Load, validate, and format quiz JSON file."""
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        print(f"❌ Error: File not found at '{file_path}'")
        return False

    print(f"📖 Reading questions file: {file_path}")
    try:
        with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error parsing JSON file: {e}")
        return False

    quizzes_to_import = []
    if isinstance(data, dict) and "quizzes" in data:
        quizzes_to_import = data["quizzes"]
    elif isinstance(data, list):
        quizzes_to_import = data
    elif isinstance(data, dict) and "questions" in data:
        # Single quiz wrapped in object
        quizzes_to_import = [data]
    else:
        print("❌ Invalid JSON format. Expected object with 'quizzes' array or list of quizzes.")
        return False

    print(f"🔍 Found {len(quizzes_to_import)} quiz(zes) to process...")

    processed_quizzes = []
    total_q_count = 0

    for i, quiz in enumerate(quizzes_to_import):
        errs = validate_quiz(quiz)
        if errs:
            print(f"\n⚠️ Validation warnings for Quiz #{i+1} ('{quiz.get('title', 'Untitled')}'):")
            for err in errs:
                print(f"   - {err}")
            continue

        q_id = quiz.get("id") or f"quiz-py-{int(time.time())}-{random.randint(1000, 9999)}"
        formatted_questions = []

        for q_idx, q in enumerate(quiz["questions"]):
            formatted_questions.append({
                "id": q.get("id") or f"q-{int(time.time())}-{q_idx+1}-{random.randint(100, 999)}",
                "type": q.get("type", "mcq"),
                "question": q["question"].strip(),
                "options": [str(opt).strip() for opt in q["options"]],
                "correct": int(q["correct"]),
                "explanation": q.get("explanation", "").strip(),
                "imageId": q.get("imageId", "")
            })

        processed_quiz = {
            "id": q_id,
            "title": quiz.get("title", "Imported Quiz").strip(),
            "category": quiz.get("category", "General").strip(),
            "difficulty": quiz.get("difficulty", "Mixed").strip(),
            "description": quiz.get("description", "Auto-imported quiz questions.").strip(),
            "timePerQuestion": int(quiz.get("timePerQuestion", 30)),
            "imageId": quiz.get("imageId", ""),
            "createdAt": quiz.get("createdAt", time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")),
            "questions": formatted_questions
        }

        processed_quizzes.append(processed_quiz)
        total_q_count += len(formatted_questions)

    if not processed_quizzes:
        print("❌ No valid quizzes could be processed.")
        return False

    # Package into database export structure
    export_db = {
        "users": [],
        "quizzes": processed_quizzes,
        "scores": [],
        "images": [],
        "materials": []
    }

    if not output_path:
        output_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "alaquizpedia_import.json")

    with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as out_f:
        json.dump(export_db, out_f, indent=2)

    print("\n" + "="*50)
    print("✅ SUCCESS! QUESTIONS PROCESSED & PACKAGED")
    print("="*50)
    print(f"📊 Total Quizzes Formatted   : {len(processed_quizzes)}")
    print(f"❓ Total Questions Processed : {total_q_count}")
    print(f"💾 Output JSON Backup File   : {output_path}")
    print("\n👉 Next Steps:")
    print(" 1. Go to your live site -> Admin Panel -> 💾 Import/Export")
    print(f" 2. Upload '{os.path.basename(output_path)}' using 'Merge' mode to add these new questions!")
    print("="*50)
    return True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- ALA QUIZPEDIA Python Question Importer ---")
    
    file_arg = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
    if not file_arg:
        default_sample = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "sample_questions.json")
        prompt = input(f"Enter path to questions JSON file (default: sample_questions.json): ").strip()
        file_arg = prompt if prompt else default_sample

    import_questions(file_arg)

# ALA QUIZPEDIA — Features Walkthrough

All requested features have been implemented and verified! Here is a summary of how everything works:

---

## 1. 📖 Public Study Materials ([materials.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/materials.html))
- **Accessible to All Users & Visitors**: Students can access study resources directly from the main navigation bar across all pages.
- **Resource Types**: Notes & Text, External Links, Video Links, and Downloadable PDFs.
- **Category & Type Filters**: Filter resources by subject (Science, History, Geography, Tech, Sports, etc.) and type.
- **Interactive Reader Modal**: Click **"📖 Read & View"** on any resource to view full notes, access video links, or download PDFs.

---

## 2. 🏆 Public Leaderboard & Shared User Performance ([leaderboard.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/leaderboard.html))
- **Admin Account Exclusion**: Admin accounts (`role === 'admin'`) are strictly excluded from leaderboard rankings and top podiums.
- **Topper Summary Header**: Displays #1 Overall Topper, Highest Accuracy Quizzer, and Most Active Quizzer.
- **Peer Performance Inspection**: Users can click on any student row or podium position to open a detailed modal showing that user's attempts, average accuracy, highest percentage, and complete attempt history!

---

## 3. 👥 Persistent User Management & Admin Performance View ([admin-users.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-users.html))
- **Admin-Only Management**: Only Admin can create, edit, or delete quizzes, study materials, and user accounts.
- **Protected Registered Users**: User accounts created during registration or by Admin remain stored and accessible until Admin explicitly chooses to delete them.
- **Detailed User Performance Inspection**: Admin can click **"📊 Performance"** next to any user to view their complete quiz history, accuracy, and attempt count.

---

## 4. 🐍 Python Question Importer Tool ([import_questions.py](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/import_questions.py))
- **JSON Question Importer**: CLI tool `import_questions.py` validates and packages quiz question JSON files (like `sample_questions.json`) into standard format (`alaquizpedia_import.json`).
- **Web JSON Import & Export**: Admins can export or import full/selected database JSON files directly on `admin-data.html`.

---

## 5. 🚀 Deploying Updates to Netlify
To deploy all latest changes to your live site (`alaquizpedia.netlify.app`), run:
```powershell
python "C:\Users\Anandhy\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\gk-quiz-platform\deploy_netlify.py"
```
Paste your Netlify Personal Access Token and press **Enter** to update your live site!

# Implementation Plan

**Goal**: Enable admin users to create custom quizzes (including custom questions) directly from the admin interface, and automatically expand the quiz catalog with new topics such as Current Affairs.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> - Confirm the UI layout for the new "Create Quiz" form (fields, order, styling). 
> - Approve the placeholder API endpoint for fetching Current Affairs data (we can replace it later with a real source).

## Open Questions
> [!WARNING]
> - Which public API (if any) should be used for pulling Current Affairs? e.g., newsapi.org, a RSS feed, etc.
> - Do you want the auto‑fetch to run on page load, on a schedule, or via a manual "Refresh" button?

## Proposed Changes
---
### Front‑end UI (admin pages)
#### [NEW] `admin-quiz-add.html`
- New admin page with a form to create a quiz (title, category, difficulty, description, time per question).
- Includes a **Create Quiz** button that saves the quiz to `localStorage` via `storage.js`.

#### [NEW] `admin-quiz-add.js`
- Handles form submission, validates inputs, constructs a quiz object with a generated ID, and calls `addQuiz` from `storage.js`.
- After creation, redirects to `admin-quiz-edit.html` for adding questions.

#### [MODIFY] `admin-quiz-edit.html`
- Add a **"Add Question"** section when a quiz is selected, with fields for:
  - Question text
  - Type (Multiple Choice / True‑False / Fill‑in‑Blank)
  - Options (dynamic list for MCQ)
  - Correct answer index/value
  - Explanation (optional)
- Hook up to a new `addQuestion` function in `storage.js`.

#### [NEW] `admin-quiz-edit.js`
- Loads selected quiz, renders existing questions, and provides UI for adding new questions.
- Calls `addQuestion(quizId, questionObj)`.

### Data Layer (storage.js)
#### [MODIFY] Add helper functions:
```js
function addQuiz(quiz) {
  const db = getDB();
  db.quizzes.push(quiz);
  saveDB(db);
  return quiz.id;
}

function addQuestion(quizId, question) {
  const db = getDB();
  const quiz = db.quizzes.find(q => q.id === quizId);
  if (!quiz) return false;
  if (!quiz.questions) quiz.questions = [];
  quiz.questions.push(question);
  saveDB(db);
  return true;
}
```
- Ensure IDs are generated via `genId('quiz')` and `genId('q')`.

### Current Affairs Auto‑Fetch
#### [NEW] `fetch_current_affairs.js`
- Simple fetch function (placeholder URL) that retrieves an array of news items.
- Transforms each item into a quiz object under category `Current Affairs` and adds it via `addQuiz`.
- Exposes a `refreshCurrentAffairs()` function that can be called manually or on a timer.

#### Integration
- Add a **"Refresh Current Affairs"** button on `admin.html` that triggers `refreshCurrentAffairs()`.
- Optionally schedule a background timer using `setInterval` (e.g., every 6 hours) to auto‑update.

## Verification Plan
### Automated Tests
- Run the existing unit‑tests (if any) and manually verify:
  1. Admin can create a new quiz and it appears in `quizzes.html`.
  2. Admin can add MCQ, True/False, and Fill‑in‑Blank questions and they work in the player.
  3. The placeholder Current Affairs fetch adds at least one quiz and it shows up.

### Manual Verification
- Log in as admin, visit `admin-quiz-add.html`, create a quiz, add questions, and play the quiz.
- Click "Refresh Current Affairs" and confirm new quizzes appear.
- Ensure the UI retains the premium visual style (gradients, glass‑morphism) consistent with the rest of the site.

---
*After your approval, I will implement the changes and redeploy the site.*

**Goal**: Enable admin users to create custom quizzes (add quizzes and questions) via the admin interface, and automatically expand the quiz catalog with new topics such as Current Affairs.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> - Approve the UI layout for the new "Create Quiz" form (fields, order, styling).
> - Approve the placeholder API endpoint for fetching Current Affairs data (can be replaced later).
> - Confirm whether the Current Affairs update should run on page load, on a schedule, or via a manual "Refresh" button.

## Open Questions
> [!WARNING]
> - Which public API should be used for pulling Current Affairs (e.g., newsapi.org, RSS feed, custom source)?
> - Desired frequency for automatic updates if using a scheduled fetch (e.g., every 6 hours).

  - Type (Multiple Choice / True‑False / Fill‑in‑Blank)
  - Options (dynamic list for MCQ)
  - Correct answer index/value
  - Explanation (optional)
- Hook up to new `addQuestion` function in `storage.js`.

#### [NEW] `admin-quiz-edit.js`
- Loads selected quiz, renders existing questions, provides UI for adding new questions.
- Calls `addQuestion(quizId, questionObj)`.

#### [MODIFY] `admin.html`
- Add **"Create New Quiz"** button linking to `admin-quiz-add.html`.
- Add **"Refresh Current Affairs"** button invoking `refreshCurrentAffairs()`.

### Data Layer (`js/storage.js`)
#### [MODIFY] Add helper functions:
```js
function addQuiz(quiz) {
  const db = getDB();
  db.quizzes.push(quiz);
  saveDB(db);
  return quiz.id;
}

function addQuestion(quizId, question) {
  const db = getDB();
  const quiz = db.quizzes.find(q => q.id === quizId);
  if (!quiz) return false;
  if (!quiz.questions) quiz.questions = [];
  quiz.questions.push(question);
  saveDB(db);
  return true;
}
```

### Current Affairs Auto‑Fetch
#### [NEW] `fetch_current_affairs.js`
- Placeholder fetch (e.g., `https://example.com/api/current-affairs`) that returns an array of news items.
- Transform each item into a quiz object under category **Current Affairs** and add via `addQuiz`.
- Export `refreshCurrentAffairs()` for manual or scheduled use.

#### Integration
- Bind **Refresh Current Affairs** button in `admin.html` to `refreshCurrentAffairs()`.
- Optionally schedule automatic updates:
```js
setInterval(refreshCurrentAffairs, 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // every 6 hours
```

### Automated Tests
- Verify `addQuiz` creates a quiz that appears on `quizzes.html`.
- Verify `addQuestion` correctly adds MCQ, True/False, and Fill‑in‑Blank questions and they work in the player.

1. Log in as admin, use **Create New Quiz**, fill the form, submit.
2. In the edit page, add several questions of varied types, save, and play the quiz from the main site.
3. Click **Refresh Current Affairs** and confirm new quizzes appear under the "Current Affairs" category.

# Implementation Plan for Admin Import/Export JSON Feature

## Goal Description

Add a new admin interface that allows an administrator to **import** quiz data from a JSON file and **export** the current quiz database to a JSON file. This will enable easy backup, migration, and bulk editing of quizzes.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This change introduces a new admin page (`admin-import-export.html`) and modifies the existing admin navigation. It also adds new JavaScript functions that interact with `localStorage`. Please review the UI design and confirm that the placement of the new admin link meets your expectations.

## Open Questions

> [!WARNING]
> - Do you want the import/export functionality to be available only to users logged in as admin (via a flag in `localStorage`) or publicly accessible?  
> - Should the exported JSON include users, scores, images, and materials, or only quizzes?

## Proposed Changes

---
### Front‑end

#### [NEW] [admin-import-export.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin-import-export.html)
* A clean, premium admin page with a dark‑mode friendly design.
* Two sections:
  * **Import** – file input (`<input type="file">`) that reads a JSON file and merges it into the existing DB via `storage.js`.
  * **Export** – a button that triggers download of the current DB as `alaquizpedia_export.json`.
* Includes helpful alerts (`[!NOTE]`) explaining the format.

#### [MODIFY] [admin.html](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/admin.html)
* Add a navigation link to the new import/export page.
* Ensure the link uses the same styling as other admin tabs.

#### [MODIFY] [js/storage.js](file:///C:/Users/Anandhy/.gemini/antagravity/scratch/gk-quiz-platform/js/storage.js)
* Expose two helper functions:
  * `importDB(jsonObj)` – validates structure and merges into the existing DB.
  * `exportDB()` – returns the full DB object for download.
* Update `getDB()` documentation.

---
### Back‑end (static site – no server code needed)
* No server‑side changes; everything runs in the browser using `localStorage`.

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
* None – the project is a static site. Manual verification will be performed.

### Manual Verification
* Open `admin.html` → click **Import/Export** link.
* Use **Export** to download a JSON file and confirm its contents match the current DB.
* Use **Import** to upload the previously downloaded file; the site should reload with the same quizzes present.
* Verify that existing quizzes are not duplicated on re‑import (id‑collision handling).
* Test on a fresh browser (no DB) – the default quiz should appear, then import adds the new data.

---
*Implementation will be performed after your approval.*

| File | Key logic | Current behaviour |
|------|-----------|-------------------|
| **js/storage.js** | `getDB()` creates a **default DB** (including a built‑in quiz) when `localStorage` is empty. | The default quiz is automatically loaded for any visitor – no login or admin rights are required. |

- The only UI element that is admin‑only is the **Admin Panel** link; it does **not** prevent regular users from accessing or playing quizzes.

### If you (or your users) are not seeing any quizzes
1. **Clear the browser’s local storage** for the site – it may contain a corrupted DB. Open the console and run:  
   ```js
   localStorage.removeItem('alaquizpedia_db');
   location.reload();
   ```
   This forces `getDB()` to recreate the default DB (including the built‑in quiz).
2. Verify that the site is loading the latest JavaScript files (clear the cache or use a hard refresh – `Ctrl+F5` on Windows).
3. If you’ve added custom quizzes via the **Import** page, make sure the JSON file follows the required structure (`users`, `quizzes`, `scores`, …). After a successful import, those quizzes will appear for **all** users.

Confirm you are okay with adding a service worker file to the project root and slightly modifying the existing HTML files. ## Open Questions > [!WARNING] > - Do you want the service worker to cache **all** static assets (HTML/CSS/JS/images) or only the core files? > - Should we inline critical CSS for the home page to reduce render‑blocking requests? ## Proposed Changes --- ### Admin Import/Export JSON (already planned) - **[NEW]** `admin-import-export.html` – premium styled admin page for JSON import/export. - **[MODIFY]** `admin.html` – add navigation link to the new import/export page. - **[MODIFY]** `js/storage.js` – expose `importDB(json)` and `exportDB()` functions (wrappers around existing `importDatabase`). - **[MODIFY]** `js/app.js` – hook UI buttons to call the new functions. --- ### Performance Enhancements - **[NEW]** `service-worker.js` – simple cache‑first service worker that pre‑caches: - `index.html`, `quizzes.html`, `quiz-player.html` - CSS `css/style.css` - JS bundle files in `js/` - Font files from Google Fonts (preconnected via ``). - Fallback network request for uncached assets. - **[MODIFY]** All HTML files (`index.html`, `quizzes.html`, `quiz-player.html`, `admin.html`, etc.): - Add `` and `` before the Google Fonts stylesheet link to reduce DNS lookup time. - Add `rel="preload" as="style"` for the main stylesheet to prioritize CSS loading. - Change script tags to `defer` (or `async` where appropriate) to avoid render‑blocking JavaScript. - Add `loading="lazy"` attribute to any `` elements (quiz cover images) to load them only when they enter the viewport. - **[MODIFY]** `js/storage.js` – add a small helper `lazyLoadImages()` using `IntersectionObserver` that replaces placeholder images with real `data-src` URLs when they become visible. - **[MODIFY]** `css/style.css` – ensure critical above‑the‑fold styles are concise; optionally move non‑critical styles to a separate file loaded asynchronously. - **[MODIFY]** `index.html` – inline a minimal CSS block for the header and navigation (critical CSS) to reduce first‑paint time. ## Verification Plan ### Automated Tests - Run `npm run lint` (if a lint script exists) to ensure no syntax errors after modifications. - Open the site in a headless browser (e.g., puppeteer) and capture the **Time to First Contentful Paint (FCP)** before and after changes to confirm improvement. ### Manual Verification - Open the site in a regular browser, clear caches, and verify: 1. The first page loads within ~1 s on a typical 3G connection. 2. Quiz images load lazily as you scroll. 3. Service worker registers (check DevTools → Application → Service Workers). 4. Offline fallback works (disable network, refresh—pages should still display). - Confirm that the admin import/export page functions correctly and that regular users can still access `quizzes.html` without any login prompts. --- *Once you approve this plan, I will implement the files, update the HTML, add the service worker, and run the verification steps.*

args.CodeContent: # Implementation Plan for Badges & Achievements Feature ## Goal Description Add a comprehensive **Badges & Achievements** system to the ALA QUIZPEDIA platform. Users will earn badges for various milestones (e.g., completing quizzes, high scores, streaks). Badges are displayed on the user profile, quiz pages, and leaderboards, enhancing engagement and providing visual rewards. ## User Review Required [!IMPORTANT] - Confirm which badge categories you want (e.g., **Quiz Completion**, **High Score**, **Streak**, **Contribution**, **Admin**, **Custom**). - Choose visual style: simple icons, text labels, or animated graphics. - Decide where badges should appear: - User profile page - Quiz results overlay - Leaderboard entries - Navbar badge indicator - Determine persistence method (localStorage for demo vs. server‑side storage if you have a backend). ## Open Questions [!WARNING] - Do you have a predefined set of badge definitions (titles, descriptions, icons)? If not, should we generate a starter set? - Should badges be **awardable only once** per user, or can they be repeatable (e.g., daily streak badge)? - Do you want **admin tools** to create/edit badges without redeploying? - Any specific achievement criteria beyond generic ones? - Should we expose an API endpoint for future integrations? ## Proposed Changes --- ### Front‑End (HTML/CSS/JS) - **new file** `badges.css` – style for badge icons, tooltips, and badge container. - **new file** `js/badges.js` – core badge logic: definitions, award checks, rendering functions. - Update `admin-profile.html` (or create if missing) to display earned badges. - Update quiz result overlay (`js/app.js` or relevant component) to show newly earned badges after a quiz. - Update leaderboard (`admin-leaderboard.html`) to show badge icons next to usernames. - Add a **Badges** navigation link in the sidebar. ### Data Model (localStorage) - Extend the stored DB schema (`storage.js`) with a new top‑level key `badges`: ```json { "badges": { "badgeId": { "title": "Quiz Master", "description": "Complete 10 quizzes", "icon": "star.svg" }, ... }, "userBadges": { "userId": ["badgeId1","badgeId2"] } } ``` - Helper functions in `storage.js`: `getUserBadges(userId)`, `addUserBadge(userId, badgeId)`. ### Badge Definitions Provide a default set (customizable): | Badge ID | Title | Criteria | Icon | |---|---|---|---| | `first_quiz` | First Quiz | Complete any quiz | `badge1.svg` | | `quiz_10` | Quiz Master | Complete 10 quizzes | `badge2.svg` | | `high_score` | High Scorer | Score ≥ 90% on a quiz | `badge3.svg` | | `streak_5` | Streak Star | 5‑day consecutive quiz attempts | `badge4.svg` | | `contributor` | Creator | Add a quiz (admin) | `badge5.svg` | ### Award Logic (in `badges.js`) - Hook into quiz completion (`saveQuizResult`) to evaluate criteria. - Hook into user registration and admin actions for relevant badges. - After awarding, update `userBadges` in storage and trigger UI render. ### UI Rendering Helpers - `renderBadge(badgeId)` – returns HTML snippet ``. - `showUserBadges(userId, containerEl)` – inject badge list. - `showEarnedBadges(badgeIds, targetEl)` – used on result page. ### Admin Badge Management (optional) - Simple JSON file `badges.json` that can be edited and re‑deployed. - Future UI could load this file dynamically for live edit. ## Verification Plan ### Automated Tests - Run existing `npm test` (if any) plus new unit tests for `badges.js`: - Award a badge when criteria met. - Prevent duplicate awards for non‑repeatable badges. - Persist badges in local storage correctly. ### Manual Verification - Register a new user, complete a quiz, and confirm the **First Quiz** badge appears on profile. - Achieve a >90% score and verify the **High Scorer** badge appears on the result overlay. - Open the leaderboard and see badge icons next to usernames. - Reload the page and ensure badges persist. --- *Please review the plan, answer the open questions, and approve before I start coding.*

# Implementation Plan – New Badge & Achievements Site (React/Next.js)

## Goal Description
Create a **stand‑alone web app** that showcases the 50 badge & achievement definitions, tracks user progress (both locally via `localStorage` and remotely via a simple backend API), and can be deployed to a hosting provider such as **Vercel** (or GitHub Pages if you prefer). The app will be built with **Next.js (React)** to allow future server‑side functionality while keeping the initial implementation lightweight.

## User Review Required
[!IMPORTANT]
- **Hosting provider** – you indicated a preference for *GitHub Pages or Vercel*. Vercel is the natural fit for Next.js; if you truly need GitHub Pages (static only) let us know and we can adjust the build.
- **Backend storage** – we will use a **Next.js API route** that writes JSON to the Vercel serverless file system (or an external stub). Confirm if a simple JSON file is acceptable for now, or if you have another storage (e.g., Supabase) in mind.
- **Design theme** – should the site use a dark‑mode glassmorphic style (as per UI guidelines) or a lighter aesthetic? Provide any brand colors or fonts you want.
- **User authentication** – Do you need login (e.g., GitHub OAuth) to associate badges across devices, or is anonymous `localStorage` sufficient for the demo?

## Open Questions
[!WARNING]
- **Icon assets** – Do you have a set of SVG badge icons ready, or should we generate placeholder icons (colored circles with the badge ID)?
- **Persistence strategy** – The plan includes both `localStorage` (fast demo) **and** a backend API that writes a `userBadges.json` file. Should the backend overwrite the file on each request, or should we implement a simple merge strategy?
- **Deploy automation** – Would you like a CI script (GitHub Actions) that runs `npm run build && vercel --prod` on push, or a manual deployment via the Vercel CLI?
- **Routing** – Desired page structure (e.g., `/`, `/badges`, `/profile`, `/leaderboard`).

## Proposed Changes
---
### Project Scaffold
- **Create new directory** `C:\Users\Anandhy\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\badge-site`.
- Run `npx -y create-next-app@latest ./` inside that folder (non‑interactive).
- Choose **JavaScript** (no TypeScript) unless you request otherwise.
- Install additional dependencies:
  - `styled-components` (or plain CSS) for premium UI.
  - `axios` for API calls.
  - `react-icons` for placeholder icons.

### Data Model
- `data/badges.json` – static file containing the 50 badge definitions (ID, title, description, repeatable flag, icon filename).
- `pages/api/userBadges.js` – API route handling `GET` (read user badge list) and `POST` (add a new badge). Data stored in `data/userBadges.json` (Vercel serverless file). For a production‑grade solution you can swap this out later.
- Front‑end helper `utils/storage.js`:
  - `loadLocalBadges()` – reads from `localStorage`.
  - `saveLocalBadges(badges)` – writes to `localStorage`.
  - `syncWithBackend()` – POSTs new badges to the API and merges response.

### Core UI Components
- **BadgeCard** – displays badge icon, title, description, earned state.
- **BadgeGrid** – responsive grid showing all 50 badges (filter by earned/unearned).
- **ProfilePage** – shows user’s earned badges and a progress summary.
- **LeaderboardPage** – mock leaderboard that reads from a static `leaderboard.json` (optional). Shows badge icons next to usernames.
- **Navbar** – includes a badge counter (e.g., 🏆 12) and links to Home, Badges, Profile.

### Styling (Premium Design)
- Add `styles/global.css` with a **dark‑mode glassmorphism** palette (e.g., HSL primary 210°, 30%, 15% background, translucent cards). Use Google Font **Inter**.
- Add `components/BadgeCard.module.css` for hover micro‑animations (scale‑up, subtle shadow).

### Award Logic
- On each quiz‑completion simulation (we’ll provide a dummy “Take Quiz” page), call `evaluateBadges(result)` which:
  1. Loads current badge list (static + user data).
  2. Checks each badge’s criteria against the result (e.g., score ≥ 90 %).
  3. If criteria met and badge not already earned (or repeatable), add to user list, update `localStorage`, and call `syncWithBackend()`.
  4. Trigger a toast notification with the newly earned badge (animated entry).

### Pages Overview
| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/` | Landing page with hero, brief intro, and “Start Quiz” button (demo). |
| `/quiz` | Simple quiz UI (hard‑coded sample questions) that returns a result object. |
| `/badges` | Full badge catalog – grid view, filter toggles (earned / all). |
| `/profile` | User profile showing earned badges and stats. |
| `/leaderboard` (optional) | Demo leaderboard with badge icons. |

### Deployment
- Add `vercel.json` to configure the API route.
- Commit the repo to a new GitHub repository (we can create it automatically via the CLI if you provide a repo name).
- Run `vercel --prod` from the project root (requires Vercel CLI token – we’ll ask you to paste it). Alternatively, enable GitHub Actions that deploy on push.

## Verification Plan
### Automated Tests
- `npm test` (Jest + React Testing Library) covering:
  - Badge data loads correctly from `badges.json`.
  - `evaluateBadges` awards a badge when criteria satisfied.
  - Duplicate award prevention for non‑repeatable badges.
  - API route returns correct JSON and writes to `userBadges.json`.

### Manual Verification
- Deploy the site to Vercel.
- Open the site, take the demo quiz, achieve a >90 % score.
- Confirm a **High Scorer (90 %)** badge appears on the Profile page and persists after a page reload.
- Verify that the badge also appears in the backend JSON via the API (`GET /api/userBadges`).
- Test the “Daily Streak” badge by simulating consecutive days (we can adjust the stored date manually). 
- Check UI responsiveness on mobile and desktop.

---
*Please review the plan, answer the open questions, and approve before I start building the new site.*

# Modern Futuristic Badge Catalog

## Goal Description
Create a premium, **modern & futuristic** badge catalog website that showcases the 50 achievement badges for the GK Quiz Platform. The site will use a **Neon cyber‑punk palette** (bright magentas, electric blues, glowing neon accents on a dark background), have **three distinct pages** (Home, Badges Gallery, About/Contact), and include an **automatic dark‑mode toggle**. The site will be built with **Next.js** (static export) and deployed to Netlify alongside the existing quiz platform.

---
## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The following decisions require your confirmation before we proceed:
>
> - **Node.js availability** – Do you have Node ≥ 14 and npm installed on this machine? If not, we can install them (requires permission).
> - **Netlify site structure** – Should the Next.js catalog be deployed as a **separate Netlify site** (its own domain) or as a **sub‑path** of the existing quiz site? (e.g., `your‑site.netlify.app/badges`)
> - **Build handling** – Do you prefer the deployment script to run `npm run build && npm run export` locally before zipping, or rely on Netlify’s build pipeline via a `netlify.toml`?

---
## Open Questions
> [!WARNING]
> - **Node.js installation** – If Node is missing, we need your permission to install it.
> - **Netlify token scope** – The provided token will be used for both sites; confirm this is acceptable.

---
## Proposed Changes

### Quiz Platform (gk-quiz-platform)
- **[MODIFY]** `data/badges.json` – Populate with 50 badge objects (id, name, description, criteria, imagePath).
- **[NEW]** `public/badges/` – Add 50 generated badge PNGs using the neon cyber‑punk theme.
- **[MODIFY]** `badge.js` & `css/badges.css` – Refine UI to match the neon aesthetic (glowing borders, gradient overlays).
- **[MODIFY]** `js/storage.js` – Ensure `loadBadges()` reads the new JSON and updates local storage on quiz events.
- **[MODIFY]** `badges.html` – Add “Earned” filter toggle, empty‑state handling, and responsive grid.

---
### Premium Next.js Badge Catalog (gk-badge-next)
- **[NEW]** `gk-badge-next/` – Full Next.js project scaffold (created manually without `npx`).
- **[NEW]** `pages/_app.js` – Global CSS import, Google Font **Inter**, dark‑mode provider.
- **[NEW]** `pages/index.js` – Hero section with animated neon gradient background and CTA to “Explore Badges”.
- **[NEW]** `pages/badges.js` – Server‑side fetch (or copy) of `../gk-quiz-platform/data/badges.json` and render using `<BadgeCard>`.
- **[NEW]** `pages/about.js` – Simple contact/about page.
- **[NEW]** `components/BadgeCard.js` – Card component with glass‑morphism, neon glow on hover, responsive layout.
- **[NEW]** `public/badges/` – Copy of the 50 badge icons.
- **[NEW]** `styles/globals.css` – Design tokens for the neon cyber‑punk palette, dark‑mode variables, smooth scroll.
- **[NEW]** `netlify.toml` – Define `build = "npm run export"`, `publish = "out"` to let Netlify handle static build.
- **[NEW]** `package.json` – Dependencies: `next`, `react`, `react-dom`; scripts: `dev`, `build`, `export`.

---
### Deployment Automation
- **[MODIFY]** `deploy_netlify.py` – Add `--project <path>` flag to zip any folder.
- **[NEW]** `deploy_quiz.bat` – Calls `python deploy_netlify.py --project gk-quiz-platform`.
- **[NEW]** `deploy_badge_next.bat` – Runs `npm install && npm run export && python deploy_netlify.py --project gk-badge-next`.
- **[MODIFY]** `.env` – Ensure `NETLIFY_TOKEN` is loaded for both deployments.

---
## Verification Plan
### Automated Tests
- `npm run build` → exit code 0.
- `npm run export` → creates `out/` with static files.
- `python deploy_netlify.py --dry-run --project <path>` → verifies zip creation.

### Manual Verification
- Open `http://localhost:3000` (dev) and `http://localhost:3000/badges` – confirm all 50 badges display with neon effects and hover animations.
- Complete a few quizzes, earn badges, and verify they appear as “earned” on both the quiz’s `badges.html` and the Next.js gallery.
- Run the two batch deployment scripts; after each finishes, open the Netlify URLs to validate responsive design on desktop & mobile, dark‑mode toggle, and correct asset loading.

---
### Timeline (approx.)
1. Install Node/npm (if needed). – 5 min.
2. Generate 50 badge icons (neon style) – 2 min per batch (total ~2 min using image generator).
3. Populate `badges.json` – <1 min.
4. Scaffold Next.js project & add components – ~10 min.
5. Update deployment scripts – 2 min.
6. Local testing & Netlify deploy – ~5 min.

**Total estimated effort:** ~30 minutes.

---
*Once you approve the plan and answer the open questions, I will begin execution.*

args.CodeContent:
# Advanced Modern Futuristic GK Platform

## Goal Description
Create a **single, high‑quality web platform** that includes:
1. An **admin panel** where the admin can:
   - Create user accounts (email & password).
   - Add new quizzes (question set, answers, categories).
2. A **login system** for regular users that loads the admin‑generated accounts from `users.json` and stores the session in `localStorage`.
3. **Quiz pages** that load the combined list of built‑in quizzes and admin‑added quizzes from `quizzes.json` so every user sees newly added quizzes instantly.
4. A **badge/achievement system** with 50 neon‑cyber‑punk badge icons, stored in `badges.json`.
5. A **Next.js badge catalog** (named `gk-badge-next`) with a futuristic glass‑morphism UI, dark‑mode toggle, and responsive badge cards.
6. **Netlify CI/CD** for two sites (the main quiz platform and the Next.js catalog) using the provided Netlify token.
7. **Robust error handling**: all scripts validate inputs, use `try/catch`, and display user‑friendly messages; linting and automated tests will be run before deployment.

---

## Open Questions (needs user confirmation)
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The following decisions affect the final implementation.

1. **Node.js installation** – Is Node.js already present on your machine? If not, may I install it via `nvm`/`chocolatey`?
2. **Netlify deployment** – Deploy the badge catalog as a **separate Netlify site** (recommended) or as a **sub‑path** of the existing quiz site?
3. **Build strategy** – Should we run `npm run build && npm run export` locally before zipping, or let Netlify build from a `netlify.toml`?
4. **Password storage** – Store passwords in plain text (simpler) or hash them client‑side (e.g., SHA‑256) before saving to `users.json`?
5. **User progress persistence** – Keep each user’s quiz results only in `localStorage`, or also store a shared `progress.json` that the admin can inspect?

---

## Proposed Changes
### 1. Core Quiz Platform (static site)
- **[NEW]** `admin.html`, `admin.css`, `admin.js` – admin UI with account creation and quiz creation forms.

If you cannot find it at the path above, or if you want to confirm exactly where it is on your system, you can use these methods:

# Goal: Advanced Modern Futuristic GK Platform

Create a premium‑looking, fast, and feature‑rich web experience that combines the existing quiz platform with a new badge‑catalog built with Next.js. The admin panel must be able to add quizzes that appear instantly for users, and users earn badge icons shown in a futuristic gallery.

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> - Confirm the Netlify site names for the **quiz platform** and the **badge catalog** (e.g., `gk-quiz` and `gk-badges`).
> - Approve the chosen color palette and Google Font (default: Inter). If you prefer a different palette, let me know.
> - Decide whether badge icons should be generated now (placeholder neon icons) or supplied later.

---
### 1. Scaffold Badge Catalog (Next.js)
- **[NEW] gk-badge-next/** – run `npx -y create-next-app@latest .` inside this folder.

### Why you should avoid this:
*   **System Protection:** The `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps` folder is a highly restricted, protected system directory owned by the TrustedInstaller service. It is designed specifically for Microsoft Store applications (MSIX/Appx packages) and is not intended for manual file storage or standard `exe`/`msi` installations.
*   **Permission Issues:** Even with Administrator privileges, you will likely encounter "Access Denied" errors. Modifying permissions on this folder to force an installation can cause system instability, break the Windows Store, or lead to application update failures.
*   **Package Compatibility:** The `--location` flag in `winget` is supported, but its success depends on the installer itself. Most installers for NodeJS will not support, nor should they be forced into, this protected system directory.

### How to use `winget` with a custom location
If your goal is simply to install NodeJS to a directory other than the default (e.g., `D:\DevTools\NodeJS`), you can use the `--location` flag. Please note that not all packages support this flag, as it depends on the underlying installer's capabilities.

To attempt an installation in a custom location, use the following syntax:

1.  **Use the default location:** By default, NodeJS installs to `C:\Program Files\nodejs`. This is the standard practice and ensures that the PATH environment variables are set correctly so that commands like `node` and `npm` work immediately in your terminal.

```python
import os
import sys
import zipfile
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
import json
import io

def create_zip_of_directory(directory_path):
    print(f"Zipping directory: {directory_path}...")
    mem_zip = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(mem_zip, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory_path):
            if '.git' in root or '__pycache__' in root or 'node_modules' in root:
                continue
            for file in files:
                if file.endswith(".py"):  # Exclude python deploy scripts
                    continue
                file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
                arcname = os.path.relpath(file_path, directory_path)
                zf.write(file_path, arcname)
    return mem_zip.getvalue()

def update_netlify_site(token, site_id, directory_path):
    zip_data = create_zip_of_directory(directory_path)

    print(f"Pushing files to Netlify Site: {site_id}...")
    deploy_url = f"https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites/{site_id}/deploys"
    deploy_headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Content-Type": "application/zip"
    }
    
    req_deploy = urllib.request.Request(deploy_url, headers=deploy_headers, data=zip_data, method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req_deploy) as response:
            deploy_info = json.loads(response.read().decode('utf-8'))
            print("-" * 40)
            print("🚀 UPDATE SUCCESSFUL! 🚀")
            print(f"Site URL: {deploy_info.get('ssl_url', deploy_info.get('url'))}")
            print("-" * 40)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        print(f"Failed to deploy: {e.read().decode('utf-8')}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- Netlify Python Deployer ---")
    
    token = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else input("Enter Netlify Access Token: ").strip()
    site_id = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "alaquizpedia.netlify.app"
    
    current_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    update_netlify_site(token, site_id, current_dir)
```
